# User guide: The wiki

## In plain words

The wiki is the living documentation of a project. People and agents keep it up to date as the project changes. A note in the Notebook is short-lived. You read it, answer it and archive it. A wiki page stays and grows. The wiki shows its pages as a tree, and the links between the pages draw the tree. You open the wiki from the Notebook drawer, or from its own page in the Unraid Tasks menu. This plugin keeps its own architecture pages and these user guides in a wiki.

## Where to find it

- **In the Notebook drawer.** Press the **Wiki** button in the drawer header. The button has a network icon. A number on the button counts the wiki pages that need your attention. Press the button again to return to your notes. A pinned drawer has the button in its row of icons at the top. In that row the button reads **Back to your notes** while the wiki view shows.
- **As its own page.** Turn on the setting **Show the Wiki as its own page**. Reload the Unraid page. A **Wiki** item shows in the **Tasks** menu. See "The Wiki page" below.
- **From the Notes list.** A wiki page is never listed in **Inbox**, **Working** or **Notes**. Only the **Archive** area lists archived wiki pages.

For the Notebook itself, see [The Notebook](notebook.md).

## How to use it

### What makes a page a wiki page

A note is a wiki page when it has the tag `wiki`. A page with the older tag `section:` and a name also counts. The home page has the tag `wiki-home`. An agent adds these tags when it makes a page. A page that other wiki pages link to is not a wiki page for that reason alone.

The wiki and the Notes list are two separate worlds. A wiki page never clutters the **Inbox**, **Working** and **Notes** areas, and a search in the list does not find one there. Use the wiki view to find wiki pages.

### The wiki view

The wiki view has two displays. A switch in its toolbar chooses between **Pages** and **Graph**. The toolbar also holds **Read all**, **Recent** and a refresh button (**Reload the wiki**).

- In a wide drawer (640 pixels or more), the toolbar sits in the drawer header, between the **Project** and **Global** switch and the icons. The header also holds the button that shows or hides the note list. The wiki view then has one bar above the content.
- In a narrow drawer or on a phone, the toolbar is one row above the content. **Read all** shows its icon only. Its text is the tooltip.

The **Pages** display shows these parts from top to bottom.

1. **The home page.** It is drawn as an ordinary page. It says what the project is and links to the main pages. If the wiki has no home page, a line says "This wiki has no home page yet" and the button **Create wiki home** makes one.
2. **Things you should know.** This part shows only when the wiki has a page of that kind. Agents add short dated lines to it for you to read. A chip counts the unread pages. **Mark all read** clears them. Each page shows its newest lines.
3. **Contents.** The tree of all wiki pages. The next section describes it.
4. **Not linked yet (N).** Wiki pages that are not in the tree. The group is closed until you open it.

### The Contents tree and links

The tree is built from the links between wiki pages. You do not sort the pages yourself. To link to a page, write its title in double square brackets in the text of another page. For example:

```
See [[Page title]] for the details.
```

A link may also have a label after a vertical bar, as in the next example. The match of the title ignores upper and lower case. A link to a title that does not exist is ignored.

```
See [[Page title|the details page]] for more.
```

The tree follows these rules:

- The first level is the home page. After it come the entry pages. An entry page is a wiki page that no other wiki page links to and that links to at least one wiki page. The newest entry pages come first.
- Under a page, the children are the wiki pages that its text links to, in the order of the links.
- Each page shows once. It sits under the first parent that reaches it. The parent closest to the top wins.
- A link back to a page that is already in the tree is ignored, so the tree has no loops.
- A link to a note that is not a wiki page does not show in the tree.

A page with children has a small arrow. The first level is open. The deeper levels are closed. A closed page shows a count such as "3 new" or "1 need you" when pages below it are New, Changed or need you. The tree supports the keyboard:

| Key | What it does |
| :-- | :-- |
| Down, Up | Move to the next or previous row. |
| Right | Open a closed page, or move to its first child. |
| Left | Close an open page, or move to its parent. |
| Home, End | Move to the first or last row. |
| Enter | Open the page. |

Each row has a menu with **Pin to the top** (or **Unpin from the top**), **Archive** and **Delete**. **Delete** shows the same pill with **Undo** as the note list. An archived page leaves the tree. Its children join another parent, or join **Not linked yet**.

### Not linked yet

A page lands under **Not linked yet (N)** when no wiki page links to it and it links to no wiki page. Open the group to see the pages. The group explains that you add a link to a wiki page, with the title of the page in double square brackets, to join the page to the tree. A page of the kind "Things you should know" or the Agent journal is not listed there.

### Open a page, Back and Close

1. Press a page in the tree, in the **Recent** list, or in a link inside another page. Expect: the page replaces the wiki view. No tab opens.
2. A strip above the page shows **Back to** the title of the previous page, the path (such as "Wiki / Page title") and a **Close this page** button.
3. Press **Back** or **Close**, or press Escape. Expect: the previous page shows. From the first page you return to the wiki home, at the place where you left it.
4. After a Back, press **Forward** (the arrow to the right of **Back to**) or press Alt+Right to return to the page you left. Alt+Left does the same as Back. **Forward** is dimmed when there is no page to go to. Opening a new page after a Back removes Forward, as in a browser.

Escape does not go back while you type in a field. Opening wiki pages never changes the open tabs of the Notes world. To read a wiki page in a tab, choose **Open in a tab** in the **More actions** menu of the page. When a page that is open is archived or deleted, the wiki goes back one step and says so. A reload of the page returns to the wiki home, because the history is kept in memory only.

### The Graph view

Press **Graph** to see which page links to which. Each page that has at least one link is a dot. A line is a link. The dot grows with the number of links. The colour shows the type of the page, and a legend names the types. A ring marks the page that is open.

- Press a dot to open the page. The keyboard works too: Tab to a dot, then Enter.
- **Zoom in** and **Zoom out** change the size of the picture.
- The picture names every page when the wiki has 40 pages or fewer. Beyond that it names the 15 busiest pages, the open page and the page under the pointer.
- Under the picture, a list repeats the pages with their number of links. The list has full-size rows for a finger.
- With no links, the view says "No links yet" and shows how to write a link.

### Unread marks and Read all

A wiki page that is **New**, **Changed** or **Needs you** shows a dot and a word. You see it in the tree, in the **Recent** list, on the home page and at the start of the line under the title of an open page. The word is there so that you do not need the colour.

- **New**: you have not read the page.
- **Changed**: the page changed after you read it.
- **Needs you**: the page waits for an answer or a comment from you.

Opening a page marks it read after about a second and a half, unless it **Needs you**. The red dot on the book tab and the number on the **Wiki** button count these pages.

**Read all** marks every New and Changed page as read, one page at a time. It shows its progress, such as "Marking 3 of 12". It then reads **All read** and stays off until a page needs reading. **Read all** leaves a **Needs you** page alone. Its tooltip says so. If a page cannot be marked, the wiki says "Could not mark some pages. They stay highlighted. Press Read all to try again."

### Make a wiki page and link it from a parent

1. Open the wiki view.
2. Press **New wiki page**, under **Contents**. Expect: a list of standard pages opens, each with a short hint. The list holds **Decisions log**, **Runbooks**, **Glossary**, **Known issues**, **Gotchas**, **How things work**, **Who owns what** and **Things you should know**. A page that already exists is left out. When all of them exist, the button is not shown.
3. Choose a page. Expect: the wiki makes the page with the tag `wiki`.
4. Open the page that should be the parent. Press **Edit in the editor** (in the Notebook drawer of a workspace).
5. Write the title of the new page in double square brackets, in a sentence. Save the file.
6. Press **Reload the wiki** if the tree has not changed. Expect: the new page shows under its parent.

Until you link it, the page shows under **Not linked yet**. Use **More actions**, **Rename...** to give a page another title. Rename the page first, and then write the link with the new title. A link with the old title does not match the page.

### The Recent popover

Press **Recent** (the clock icon) to see the 10 wiki pages that changed last. Each line shows the title, the type, the time and the flag. A number on the button counts the New and Changed pages in the list. Press a page to open it. Escape closes the list. The button shows only when the wiki has two pages or more.

### Properties and Linked from

Every page has a **Properties** button (the "i" icon). The panel shows the type, the area, who made and changed the page, the dates, the file path, the id, the version and the tags. A section **Linked from (N)** lists the pages that link here. Press a name to open that page. The section is closed at first and shows only when a page links here. **More actions** also has **Linked from (N)**, which opens the panel with the section open.

### The compact header

An open page has a header of two lines. The first line holds the title and the action buttons. The second line holds the flag, the time of the last update and **Not committed** when the file differs from the last git commit. The rest is in **Properties**. In a header narrower than 760 pixels, **Read aloud**, **Ask the agent to refresh this note**, **History**, **Go to comments** and **Properties** move into the **More actions** menu. The title may use two lines.

### The Wiki page

The setting **Show the Wiki as its own page** adds a **Wiki** item to the **Tasks** menu. You read the wiki there without a terminal.

1. Open the plugin settings, the **Configuration** tab, the **Notebook** card.
2. Set **Show the Wiki as its own page** to **On**.
3. Reload the Unraid page. Expect: **Wiki** shows in the **Tasks** menu.
4. Open **Wiki**. A **Project** list at the top picks the project. It names each project folder that has a Notebook, by the names of its workspaces, and it offers **Global**.

The list shows a project only when its notebook folder exists. A project whose workspaces are all deleted is not listed. **Global** is always the last entry. The page remembers your choice in the browser and in the address (the part after `?project=`). A link to the page opens the same project. If a project is not in the list, the page says so and shows the first project.

The page is the real Notebook in a wide layout. It starts on the wiki view. The note list, open pages, search, comments, history, new notes, archive and delete all work. A project whose workspaces are stopped still shows. The page works with the Unraid login, like every page of the plugin. A change that you make on the page shows in the drawer of a terminal, and a change in the drawer shows on the page.

On the Wiki page, **Edit in the editor** stays off, because the file editor belongs to the terminal page. To change the text of a page, use the Notebook drawer of a workspace in that project.

With the setting **Off**, the **Wiki** item is hidden. The address of the page then shows one sentence: "The Wiki page is turned off. A person turns it on in Settings, Notebook." It shows no notes.

### The architecture pages and these user guides

This plugin keeps its own documentation in a wiki. The wiki lives in the Notebook of the plugin's project. The pages are files in the notebook folder, so git keeps them. They are:

- These user guides. Start at [User guide](README.md).

The same rules apply to every page. A page opens with "In plain words", a short text for a reader who is not an engineer. A page ends with a collapsed **Change history** block that lists what changed and when. The page text always describes the current behaviour. A change to the code and the change to its page go into the same commit. A check, run by the plugin's test tools, finds a page that has fallen behind its code.

### Voice mail copies are ordinary notes

When both Voice and the Notebook are on, the plugin copies every voice mail message into the Notebook of the speaking workspace's project. Each copy is a note with a title that starts "Voice mail:" and the first words of the message. The note is in the **Notes** area and has the tags `voicemail` and a message id. It is not a wiki page. It shows in the Notes list, not in the wiki view. You archive and delete it like any note. Deleting or clearing the voice mail message does not remove the note. See [Voice](voice.md).

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Show the Wiki as its own page** | Adds a **Wiki** item to the **Tasks** menu. The page holds the Notebook of a project, with the wiki view first. | Off | Turn it on when you want to read or edit the wiki without a terminal. Reload the Unraid page after the change. |
| **Notebook** | Turns the whole Notebook on or off, including the wiki view and the Wiki page. | On | Turn it off only if you do not want agents to use a Notebook. |
| **Agent journal** | Lets agents keep a timeline note. The journal is not listed under **Not linked yet**. | Off | See [The Notebook](notebook.md). |

## What happens behind the scenes

The wiki is not a separate store. A wiki page is an ordinary Notebook file with the tag `wiki`. The plugin reads the links in the text of all wiki pages and builds the tree, the **Not linked yet** group and the graph from them. The tree is rebuilt whenever a page changes. See C4 Component: React Terminal Spa and C4 Component: Server Rendered Ui.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| "This wiki has no home page yet" | No page has the tag `wiki-home`. | Press **Create wiki home**. |
| A page is missing from the tree | No wiki page links to it. | Look under **Not linked yet (N)**. Add a link to the page in a parent page. |
| A page is missing from the wiki view | The page has no `wiki` tag, or it is archived. | Look in the **Archive** area. Ask the agent that made the page to tag it. |
| A new link does not show in the tree | The tree is read again after a page changes. | Press **Reload the wiki**. Check that the title matches the page title. |
| **New wiki page** is not shown | All standard pages exist. | Make the page in another way, or rename a standard page. |
| The tree keeps a page under the wrong parent | A page shows under the first parent that reaches it. | Remove the link from the wrong parent, or link it from the parent that you want to be first. |
| No **Wiki** item in the **Tasks** menu | The setting is **Off**, or the page was not reloaded. | Turn on **Show the Wiki as its own page** and reload the Unraid page. |
| "The Notebook is switched off" on the Wiki page | The setting **Notebook** is **Off**. | Follow the link on the page and turn the setting on. |
| "No project has a Notebook yet" | No workspace has a notebook folder yet. | Let an agent make a note in a project, or use the **Global** Notebook. |
| "Could not mark some pages" | A **Read all** request failed. | Press **Read all** again. |
